title: Stool test for parasites (ova and parasites)
what: At home, you collect a little stool in a special container. In the lab, it is checked under a microscope for worm eggs and other parasites.
why: For certificates for kindergarten, school, or a pool; or for belly pain, itching, loose stools, or poor appetite.
duration: collecting at home takes a few minutes; results usually come in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: If you take or recently took worm medicines or antibiotics
If you recently had an X-ray with contrast

prepare.title: Container
prepare.text: Get a sterile container with a small scoop from the lab or a pharmacy. Sometimes the container has liquid inside. Do not pour it out.

prepare.title: Collecting
prepare.text: Collect stool from a natural bowel movement, without enemas or laxatives. Keep urine out of the container.

prepare.title: Storage
prepare.text: Take it to the lab the same day, usually within a few hours. Ask the lab how to store it.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take.

steps: Pass stool into a clean, dry pot or a bag, not into the toilet water
Use the scoop in the lid to take a little stool from different spots
Fill the container about one third full
Close it tightly and label it
Take it to the lab within the time you were given
feel: Nothing unpleasant, just a little awkward
after: Results usually come in 1 to 3 days
Sometimes the doctor asks for 2 or 3 samples. This makes finding parasites more likely

faq.q: Why repeat the test if nothing was found?
faq.a: Eggs do not come out every day. So the test is sometimes done several times, a few days apart.

faq.q: Can I collect stool in the evening and bring it in the morning?
faq.a: It depends on the lab and the type of container. Ask in advance.

reminders.text: Stool test for parasites tomorrow. Get the container and a clean pot or bag ready.
